coverage: Source-controlled directory; not an exhaustive list of distinct physical beaches

beaches.name: Agawa Bay, Lake Superior Provincial Park
beaches.story: A wide sweep of shingle and sand faces Lake Superior. When the wind moves off open water, the beach may feel very different from the wooded campground behind it. Listen to the waves as the wooded campground opens onto Superior's shore. Compare the breeze among the trees with the air over the sand before choosing your place.

beaches.name: Awenda Provincial Park, Georgian Bay Beaches
beaches.story: Trails pass through forest before reaching a series of Georgian Bay beaches. The trees offer shelter on the way down, but the shoreline opens to wind, islands and broad water views. The forested approach leads to several shores with different exposure. Use the park map to choose your beach, then observe which way the breeze crosses Georgian Bay.

beaches.name: Batchawana Bay Provincial Park
beaches.story: At this broad Lake Superior bay, the sand and shallow water sit beneath a wooded shoreline. Look across the bay before you settle in: wind coming off the open lake can feel unlike the air under the trees. Trees and open bay create two different wind settings. Notice whether the air reaches you from across Superior and check Ontario Parks' latest beach information.

beaches.name: Bay Beach, Crystal Beach
beaches.story: The sandy north shore of eastern Lake Erie opens to a broad sweep of water. Before entering the lake, check both the wind and the Niagara Region's current beach results. The sand meets a broad sweep of eastern Lake Erie. A refreshing breeze does not say anything about bacteria; consult Niagara Region's beach results separately.

beaches.name: Bayfield Pier Beach
beaches.story: Just outside Bayfield's river mouth, the pier and beach face the westward sweep of Lake Huron. A breeze along the open waterfront can be different from the air among the village shops. The village streets offer shelter the open pier may not. Notice the wind direction by Lake Huron and take care around channel currents.

beaches.name: Victoria Park Beach, Cobourg
beaches.story: From the lawns of Victoria Park, the shore opens to Lake Ontario. The water can be a welcome contrast to town heat, while the open beach brings its own wind. Leave the lawns of Victoria Park and face Lake Ontario. The breeze across the sand may differ from town air. Read the local beach notices before swimming.

beaches.name: Darlington Provincial Park, Lake Ontario Beach
beaches.story: Past the park's woods and meadows, a sandy Lake Ontario shore opens onto the horizon. The breeze across the lake may differ from the weather along nearby city streets. Meadows and woods open onto a wide Lake Ontario horizon. Feel the change in wind when you step onto the sand, then compare it with the nearby forecast.

beaches.name: Grand Bend Main Beach
beaches.story: On Lake Huron's eastern shore, the dune fringe gives way to a lively town beach. Watch the flags and wind before you decide how long to linger near the water. Busy streets and an open Lake Huron beach sit side by side. Notice whether the wind arrives across the water, and consult the posted flags before entering.

beaches.name: Inverhuron Provincial Park
beaches.story: Among dunes and young forest, Inverhuron's beach opens west toward Lake Huron sunsets. Open sand offers less shelter from a rising breeze. This west-facing shore can be especially inviting as afternoon light changes. Check the wind and temperature forecast for your return as well as your arrival.

beaches.name: Katherine Cove, Lake Superior Provincial Park
beaches.story: The shoreline folds into a sheltered cove of clear water and rounded stone. Step beyond the trees and listen for the wind crossing the lake. This cove invites a careful look at how rock headlands shape a shore. Some wind directions may be sheltered, others not. The actual waves tell today's story.

beaches.name: Killbear Provincial Park, Georgian Bay
beaches.story: Smooth rock, sandy coves and wind-shaped pines share this Georgian Bay peninsula. One small bay may feel sheltered while a nearby point faces the wind. Use the park map to choose your shore. Compare the water behind a rock point with waves beyond it. That small difference in shelter can change the experience, but it never guarantees swimming safety.

beaches.name: Station Beach, Kincardine
beaches.story: The sand lies below Kincardine's lighthouse and waterfront boardwalk. Onshore wind can make this reach feel much cooler than town; look for the municipality's Smart Beach Light information as well as health notices. The lighthouse and boardwalk help you read the shoreline. Watch the angle of arriving waves and consult municipal beach guidance and public-health notices.

beaches.name: Long Point Provincial Park
beaches.story: The sandy peninsula stretches far into Lake Erie, with dunes, marsh and abundant birdlife. On an exposed shore, a breeze is part of the landscape. The peninsula reaches far into Lake Erie and is exposed to changing wind directions. Read the shoreline conditions for the section you plan to visit, not just the nearby town.

beaches.name: Neys Provincial Park
beaches.story: On Ashburton Bay, broad sand lies beneath the rocky hills of Superior's north shore. Even a sunny day can bring a cool breath off the lake. Rocky hills rise behind the sand while Superior's cold expanse lies ahead. If air crosses the lake toward you, it may feel different from a warmer inland forecast.

beaches.name: North Beach Provincial Park
beaches.story: A slender sandy barrier separates Lake Ontario from North Bay. The open lakeside beach and sheltered bay shore may feel different on the same visit. This narrow barrier has an open-lake side and a bay side. See how the water and breeze differ between them, and follow park guidance for access and swimming.

beaches.name: Old Woman Bay, Lake Superior Provincial Park
beaches.story: The beach bends below steep rock headlands at the mouth of the Old Woman River. When the bay is windy, you can hear surf on the stones even before you leave the highway-side forest. Take in the headlands from the beach, then watch the surf below them. Dramatic cliffs do not mean the water is sheltered from every wind.

beaches.name: Pancake Bay Provincial Park
beaches.story: A long pale beach curves around Pancake Bay beneath coastal forest. In this sheltered bay, the lake's wide horizons and the air over the sand tell different parts of the weather story. Follow the curve of the sand with your eyes. Its shape creates different angles to the wind along the same bay. Check the current park information before going into the water.

beaches.name: Pinery Provincial Park
beaches.story: Walk through oak savanna and dunes, then emerge onto the open Lake Huron beach. Here the wind may change as abruptly as the landscape. The oak savanna and dunes create a sheltered approach to the open lake. Feel how the breeze changes as you step onto the sand and note which way it is coming from.

beaches.name: Port Burwell Provincial Park
beaches.story: A wide sandy shoreline faces the open waters of Lake Erie. Wind and waves can change quickly here; a clear sky is not a swimming-safety report. The big sky makes wind and clouds easy to notice here. Let the forecast help plan the day, but use posted park information for access and swimming.

beaches.name: Port Stanley Main Beach
beaches.story: Beyond the harbor, Port Stanley's wide sand faces Lake Erie. The breeze can be stronger by the water than among the village streets. The harbor and open beach are neighbors, but moving water near a channel deserves its own caution. Watch the waves beyond the pier and check official notices.

beaches.name: Presqu'ile Provincial Park
beaches.story: Dunes and marsh frame one of Lake Ontario's long sandy shores. Watch the weather move across the open lake, and listen for birds behind the beach. Listen for birds inland, then turn to the waves beyond the dunes. The marsh and the beach offer different shelter from the same wind.

beaches.name: Rondeau Provincial Park, Lake Erie Beach
beaches.story: Along the Erie side of the Rondeau peninsula, stretches of sand border Carolinian forest. A wind that barely stirs the trees can build waves along the open beach. Walk from the Carolinian forest toward the Lake Erie sand. The air may feel quite different when the tree cover ends. Check posted park conditions.

beaches.name: Sandbanks Provincial Park, Lakeshore Beach
beaches.story: The great dune country of Prince Edward County meets Lake Ontario at Lakeshore Beach. Far across the water, the horizon gives no sign of how quickly an afternoon wind can shift. From the dunes the horizon seems endless. Notice the transition from sheltered sand to open wind near Lake Ontario, then compare that experience with the forecast.

beaches.name: Sauble Beach
beaches.story: Lake Huron spreads to the western horizon beyond this broad strand. The beach is not just the forecast in town: the lake and wind direction matter. Note that some nearby shore sections are known as Saugeen Beach; follow current local access rules. Watch the direction of waves along the wide strand. A warm day in town may feel different beside Lake Huron. Confirm the specific beach section's current access guidance.

beaches.name: Terrace Bay Beach
beaches.story: Follow the mouth of the Aguasabon River toward the open Lake Superior horizon. From the sand you can look toward the Slate Islands; check the wind and the district beach notices before spending time at the waterline. The Aguasabon River joins the landscape at the water's edge. Look toward the Slate Islands, then study waves near shore; river mouths have separate current concerns.

beaches.name: Bluffer's Park Beach, Toronto
beaches.story: The great Scarborough bluffs rise behind this sandy Lake Ontario beach. At the foot of the cliffs, wind and waves can feel a world apart from the neighborhoods above. The high Scarborough Bluffs frame the sand dramatically. They may shelter some approaches without protecting the beach from every wind; follow established public access routes.

beaches.name: Cherry Beach, Toronto
beaches.story: The sheltered city streets give way to a strip of sand along Toronto's Port Lands waterfront. Watch the wind across Lake Ontario and consult the city's beach program before entering the water. The Port Lands streets give way to sand and open lake. Notice the change in breeze, and consult Toronto's current beach monitoring for swimming information.

beaches.name: Woodbine Beach, Toronto
beaches.story: City streets give way to open sand and Lake Ontario at Woodbine. The lakeshore can feel cooler than the nearby neighborhoods, but only a verified forecast belongs on the temperature card. A few streets separate city warmth from open Lake Ontario wind. Compare those settings on your visit and use Toronto's beach reports rather than relying on weather alone.

beaches.name: Turkey Point Beach
beaches.story: The village beach looks across a broad, shallow part of Lake Erie. Shallow water does not guarantee calm water: check the current signs and wind before choosing a swimming spot. The water may appear gentle here, but a shallow lake can still have hazards. Watch the waves and read current park notices before entering.

beaches.name: Wasaga Beach Provincial Park
beaches.story: The long sand shore meets Georgian Bay, part of Lake Huron. Even with warm streets behind you, the air over the broad bay can set its own pace. The long beach stretches across Georgian Bay's horizon. Walk a short distance and notice how the breeze and waves meet the sand; a city-area forecast cannot resolve every local difference.

beaches.story: A quieter sand-and-cobble shoreline between Rogers City and Forty Mile Point.

beaches.name: Lakeport State Park
beaches.story: An open Lake Huron beach north of Port Huron with clear, usually cooler water.

beaches.name: Ludington State Park
beaches.story: A long dune-backed beach between Lake Michigan and Hamlin Lake, with Big Sable Point Lighthouse to the north.

beaches.name: McLain State Park
beaches.story: A dramatic Keweenaw beach known for open-water sunsets and cold, clear Lake Superior water.

beaches.name: Muskegon State Park
beaches.story: Two miles of Lake Michigan beach with channel views and room to spread out.

beaches.name: New Buffalo Beach
beaches.story: Michigan's southernmost major Lake Michigan town beach and an easy trip from Chicago.

beaches.name: North Bar Lake
beaches.story: A small inland lake separated from Lake Michigan by a narrow sand bar.

beaches.name: Oscoda Beach Park
beaches.story: A broad Sunrise Coast beach with a pier, playground, and downtown Oscoda nearby.

beaches.name: Pentwater Beach
beaches.story: A walkable harbor-town beach beside the Pentwater channel and pier.

beaches.name: Petoskey State Park
beaches.story: A Little Traverse Bay beach known for clear water and Petoskey stones.

beaches.name: P.J. Hoffmaster State Park
beaches.story: Three miles of undeveloped shoreline backed by a dramatic dune system.

beaches.name: Port Crescent State Park
aliases: Port Crescent State Park - Day Use
beaches.story: Three miles of sandy Lake Huron shoreline near the tip of Michigan's Thumb.

beaches.name: Presque Isle Park
beaches.story: Marquette's signature Lake Superior park, with rocky shoreline, coves, and harbor-side beach access.

beaches.name: Lakeside Park Beach
beaches.story: A sandy municipal beach and waterfront park in downtown Rogers City.

beaches.name: Sand Point Beach
beaches.story: A shallow-water township beach on the Sand Point peninsula.

beaches.name: Saugatuck Dunes State Park
beaches.story: A walk-in beach with tall dunes and lighter crowds than many West Michigan destinations.

beaches.name: Silver Lake State Park
beaches.story: Two miles of Lake Michigan shoreline beside the Silver Lake Sand Dunes.

beaches.name: South Haven North Beach
beaches.story: A wide, amenity-rich city beach at the Black River channel.

beaches.name: Tawas Point State Park
beaches.story: A long sandy point between Tawas Bay and open Lake Huron, anchored by an historic lighthouse.

beaches.name: Tunnel Park
beaches.story: A family beach north of Holland reached through a tunnel cut into the dune.

beaches.name: Twelvemile Beach
beaches.story: A long and comparatively remote sand beach in Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore.

beaches.name: Van Buren State Park
beaches.story: A mile of Lake Michigan beach and dunes south of South Haven.

beaches.name: Warren Dunes State Park
beaches.story: Three miles of beach backed by dunes rising more than 200 feet above Lake Michigan.

beaches.name: Whitefish Point
beaches.story: A cobble-and-sand shoreline beside the lighthouse, bird observatory, and Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum.

beaches.name: Wilderness State Park
beaches.story: A quieter beach at the northwest tip of the Lower Peninsula with broad western views.

beaches.name: Big Bay State Park
beaches.accessAlert: The park reports construction closures affecting the beach parking lot from September 8, 2026 through approximately June 30, 2027. Check current park conditions before travel.
beaches.story: Madeline Island's sandstone shore opens to Lake Superior. The beach and wooded boardwalk offer very different shelter from wind, even within a short walk. Walk from the wooded boardwalk toward the shoreline and notice when the shelter falls away. That change in wind can tell you more about comfort than a single inland temperature.

beaches.name: Edgewater Beach
beaches.story: Just beyond Cleveland's streets, the beach faces a broad stretch of Lake Erie. The open water and exposed sand can change how a day feels without changing the city forecast. Cleveland's skyline is the backdrop; Lake Erie is the weather-making foreground. Compare the wind among the streets with what you feel on the open sand.

beaches.name: Fair Haven Beach State Park
beaches.advisoryName: New York Coastal Beach Water Quality
beaches.story: High bluffs and sandy shoreline share a small corner of Lake Ontario. At water level you meet a different wind exposure than on paths above the beach. The bluff and beach give two levels from which to experience the same lake. Wind exposure may differ between them. Check the issued forecast and the shoreline itself.

beaches.name: Hamlin Beach State Park
beaches.advisoryName: New York Coastal Beach Water Quality
beaches.story: Lake Ontario stretches north from these broad beaches. A clear inland morning is only part of the story; the open water and the afternoon breeze matter here. Lake Ontario fills the northern horizon. Watch clouds move above the water and notice whether wind reaches the beach from the lake or across the park.

beaches.name: Indiana Dunes State Park
beaches.story: Dune ridges rise beyond a wide sandy strand. Wind crossing Lake Michigan meets a landscape of exposed shore, protected hollows and forest. The dune ridges offer pockets of shelter, but the waterline opens to the breeze. Watch the direction of the waves and ask what part of the forecast applies to this exact setting.

beaches.name: Kohler-Andrae State Park
beaches.story: Wooded trails and dune grasses give way to a long, open sweep of Lake Michigan. A breeze that barely stirs the pines may be more noticeable on the sand. Pause where dune grass gives way to open beach. A breeze crossing Lake Michigan may feel different from the air among the pines. Compare the forecast with the wind you meet here.

beaches.name: Maumee Bay State Park
beaches.story: Here Lake Erie meets marsh, meadow and shore. The western basin is shallow, and the experience may change quickly as clouds and wind pass across the bay. The marshes and exposed shore offer two neighboring experiences of the same afternoon. Look for the direction the air is moving, and remember that shallow water does not establish safe swimming.

beaches.name: Point Beach State Forest
beaches.story: Six miles of beach edge the forest. Where trees stop and open water begins, the breeze and the sounds of Lake Michigan become the weather story. Listen for the change from forest sounds to waves. Trees can soften wind that is moving freely over the lake. Consider both settings when choosing how long to stay.

beaches.name: Presque Isle State Park, Beach 6
beaches.accessAlert: Swimming is permitted only at designated guarded areas when officially open. Check current staffed beaches and posted restrictions.
beaches.story: On Presque Isle's sandy peninsula, Lake Erie is always close. The breeze you feel beyond the dunes may differ from conditions back in Erie. This peninsula turns the shoreline toward different winds. Study the waves reaching your section of beach before choosing where to linger and check the current posted guidance.

beaches.name: West Beach, Indiana Dunes National Park
beaches.story: Climb toward the dunes and you can see how much shoreline the lake controls. The open beach is less sheltered than the woods and stairs behind it. On a visit through the dunes, notice where the stairs or wooded approaches give way to the full reach of lake wind. Check the park's current access information before you set out.
